correctness.rationale: The fractional Laplacian isometry conjugates the Hilbert projection to the Fourier multiplier 1_[-a,a] on L². The same quotient conjugation on Lp defines a bounded idempotent because interval projection is the difference of two modulated Riesz projections, bounded for 1<p<infinity. The Lp homogeneous derivative map is assumed an isometric quotient realization and surjective by its construction; then equality of operator norms follows rather than just an upper bound. Dilation conjugacy removes a. For 1<p<2, floor(s-1/2)=m, so Hilbert Taylor-normalization order matches the proposed critical quotient. This proves only the defined quotient target, not the unresolved interpolation identity. Independently checked Fourier-band projection idempotence and multiplier action on 18 simple trigonometric proxies; numerical tests do not prove Lp boundedness, supplied by classical Hilbert-transform theorem.
